name: Ben-geber
overview: Ben-geber was a male figure known for serving as one of King Solomon's twelve deputies, specifically overseeing the region of Ramoth-gilead. The Scripture highlights his administrative role during Solomon's reign but does not provide further tribal or familial details beyond his duty. His position reflects the organized governance established under Solomon's kingdom.
namesAndTitles: The name Ben-geber means 'son of strength,' indicating a designation that may reflect qualities of power or reliability. This proper name, recorded in 1 Kings 4:12, is not noted as being given directly by God but carries a meaningful Hebrew significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Ben-geber was a descendant of Manasseh, linking him to one of the tribes of Israel. Beyond this ancestral connection, no additional family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Ben-geber's significance lies in his role as a key administrative official under Solomon, entrusted with governing a vital territory, Ramoth-gilead. His appointment as one of the twelve deputies demonstrates the structured and divinely sanctioned leadership within Israel during Solomon's reign. This governance contributed to the stability and prosperity described in the biblical narrative of Solomon's kingdom.
